+    under [Tachygram accumulator](draft-tachyon-shielded-protocol.md#tachygramaccumulator)
+    and [Per-stamp checks](draft-tachyon-shielded-protocol.md#per-stampchecks).

+:   As defined in [Multiset commitments](draft-tachyon-shielded-protocol.md#multisetcommitments)
+    in the Tachyon Shielded Protocol ZIP. Its application to this format is
+    described under [Multiset commitments](#multisetcommitments) below.

+    [Stamp](draft-tachyon-shielded-protocol.md#stamp) in the Tachyon Shielded Protocol ZIP.

+The remaining terms are defined by this ZIP:

+:   The Tachyon section of a transaction: actions, a value balance, a maximum-fee

+# Abstract
+
+This ZIP is a living draft and does not prescribe whether the Tachyon bundle is
+deployed through ZIP 248's extensible transaction format[^zip-0248] or incorporated
+directly into a new transaction format. Its encoding and integration details may
+be revised as ZIP 248 and other related draft ZIPs evolve.
+
+This revision follows the transaction-local tachygrams and aggregate-to-adjunct
+txid references proposed in Tachyon issue #226 and implemented in draft PR #280,
+at revision `e6bcdf1`.[^tachyon-design] [^tachyon-format-pr]
+
+This ZIP specifies the consensus wire format of the Tachyon bundle: a three-state
+discriminator byte, a common body, and a proof or stripped stamp trailer. Both
+trailers retain the bundle's own tachygrams and fee. A proof stamp additionally
+carries the proof, anchor, tachygram-union commitment, and covered-transaction list.
+It defines the canonical field encodings and sequence orders, the action and descriptor digests, and the use of the shielded protocol's multiset commitments in bundle verification.
+It further defines the bundle's transaction-digest inputs, the consensus rules scoped to a single bundle, and the block-scoped rules that validate a block's bundles together.
+It defines the transaction representation of the
+[*Tachyon pool*](draft-tachyon-shielded-protocol.md), just as ZIP 225 [^zip-0225]
+defines the v5 transaction fields for the [Orchard shielded protocol](zip-0224.rst).
+
+# Motivation
+
+To improve scalability, the [Tachyon shielded protocol](draft-tachyon-shielded-protocol.md)
+supports [proof aggregation](draft-tachyon-shielded-protocol.md#prooftree).
+A covering transaction carries a merged proof and lists the txids of the other
+transactions it covers. Those transactions retain their actions, signatures,
+tachygrams, and fees when their proofs are stripped for block inclusion.
+
+Keeping tachygrams with their originating transactions preserves their association
+for note retrieval. Binding each pair into its action digest makes that association
+verifiable. The explicit txid list identifies the transactions needed to validate
+an aggregate.[^tachyon-design]
+
+The format separates effecting data from authorization data so that aggregation
+and stripping preserve `txid` and existing signatures. A stripped bundle's bytes
+depend on that bundle alone, allowing its covering proof to change without
+rewriting a reference in the adjunct.
+
+# Requirements
+
+* A transaction's `txid` contribution is invariant across stamping, merging, stripping, and re-stamping.
+* Proof-stamped and stripped forms carry identical effecting data and signatures.
+* Stripping preserves the bundle's own tachygrams and applied fee.
+* Every field needed for signature and balance verification is present in both states.
+* Aggregate coverage is identified by an explicit list of covered transaction txids.
+* Parsers bound action counts, adjunct counts, and proof lengths before allocation.
+* Bundles with no actions are representable under both stamp forms.
+
+# Non-requirements
+
+This ZIP does not independently define:
+
+* the multiset commitment construction, which is specified in the
+  [Tachyon Shielded Protocol](draft-tachyon-shielded-protocol.md#multisetcommitments) ZIP;
+* the proof statement, which is specified in the Tachyon Shielded Protocol ZIP
+  under [Stamp](draft-tachyon-shielded-protocol.md#stamp) and
+  [Proof tree](draft-tachyon-shielded-protocol.md#prooftree);
+* the tachygram accumulator, anchor semantics and validity rules, and cross-block
+  duplicate-tachygram checks within the retained epoch window, which are specified
+  in the Tachyon Shielded Protocol ZIP under
+  [Tachygram accumulator](draft-tachyon-shielded-protocol.md#tachygramaccumulator),
+  [Epochs](draft-tachyon-shielded-protocol.md#epochs), and
+  [Per-stamp checks](draft-tachyon-shielded-protocol.md#per-stampchecks);

+# Specification

+The specification proceeds from the wire layout of the bundle body to the rules over its fields, then to the digest constructions and multiset commitment inputs those rules use, then to the two stamp forms.

+## Bundle body
+
+When `tachyonBundleState` is not `0x00`, the body follows the discriminator byte, laid out as in the wire layout above.
+
+`valueBalanceTachyon` is a two's-complement signed 64-bit integer in little-endian byte order.
+`vActionsTachyon` is a sequence of `nActionsTachyon` action descriptors, each the 32-byte encoding of $\mathsf{cv}$ followed by the 32-byte encoding of $\mathsf{rk}$.
+`vActionSigsTachyon` is a sequence of `nActionsTachyon` 64-byte signatures; the $i$-th signature authorizes the $i$-th descriptor.
+Both sequences share the single count `nActionsTachyon`, so a count mismatch between descriptors and signatures is unrepresentable.
+The descriptor sequence's order is the transaction author's choice.
+The semantics of spends and outputs are described in the shielded-protocol ZIP's
+[Proof tree](draft-tachyon-shielded-protocol.md#prooftree) section.
+
+`vMemoTachyon` is an opaque recipient-directed payload of `nMemoTachyon` bytes; `nMemoTachyon` of $0$ encodes an absent payload.
+The memo contributes to `txid` and the sighash ([Transaction digest contributions](#transactiondigestcontributions)) rather than to `auth_digest`, so it is identical across bundle states.
+
+## Value balance and the binding signature
+
+`valueBalanceTachyon` counts the maximum-fee note as an output: total value spent
+minus ordinary outputs minus the maximum fee. The applied fee is selected later,
+and the remaining value returns as a fee change note, as specified under
+[Fees](draft-tachyon-shielded-protocol.md#fees). The bundle's net pool outflow is
+`valueBalanceTachyon + vFeeTachyon`.[^tachyon-fees]
+
+Tachyon reuses Orchard's value commitments[^protocol-valuecommit] and binding
+signature construction.[^protocol-orchardbalance] The derived binding validating
+key is
+
+$$\mathsf{bvk} = \sum_i \mathsf{cv}_i + \mathsf{cv}_{\mathsf{feeMax}}
+  - [\mathsf{valueBalanceTachyon}]\mathcal{V},$$
+
+where $\mathsf{cv}_{\mathsf{feeMax}}$ is `cvFeeMaxTachyon` and $\mathcal{V}$ is
+Orchard's value generator. `bindingSigTachyon` MUST verify over the transaction
+sighash under this key. The applied fee is excluded from the binding-key derivation.
+
+## Action signatures
+
+Each action signature in `vActionSigsTachyon` MUST be a valid spend authorization signature (§ 4.15 ‘Spend Authorization Signature (Sapling and Orchard)’; RedPallas with the SpendAuth basepoint of § 5.4.7.1, for spends and outputs alike) over the transaction sighash under the corresponding action's $\mathsf{rk}$.
+All of a bundle's signatures sign the same transaction-level sighash. The
+Tachyon-specific inputs and pending integration with the ZIP 244 framework
+[^zip-0244] are described under
+[Transaction digest contributions](#transactiondigestcontributions).
+
+## Action digests
+
+Let $(\mathsf{cv}_x, \mathsf{cv}_y)$ and $(\mathsf{rk}_x, \mathsf{rk}_y)$ be the
+affine Pallas coordinates of an action's value commitment and randomized key.
+Let $t_0, t_1$ be its two Pallas base-field tachygrams, taken from the corresponding
+pair in its bundle's `vTachygrams`. Its action digest is the Pallas base-field element
+
+$$d = \mathsf{Poseidon}_{\texttt{Tachyon-ActionDg}}\bigl(
+  \mathsf{cv}_x, \mathsf{cv}_y, \mathsf{rk}_x, \mathsf{rk}_y,
+  t_0 + t_1, t_0 t_1\bigr).$$
+
+The sum and product bind the pair without distinguishing its order. The proof
+MUST bind the same pair to the action and to the covered tachygram multiset.
+The tagged Poseidon sponge initializes its rate to zero and its capacity to the
+little-endian integer represented by the domain's ASCII bytes, zero-padded to
+16 bytes, and absorbs the listed data elements.[^tachyon-poseidon]
+The [shielded protocol](draft-tachyon-shielded-protocol.md#prooftree) specifies the
+proof constraints.[^tachyon-binding]
+
+TODO: Specify the Tachyon Poseidon permutation parameters and sponge operations
+in the Zcash Protocol Specification.
+
+If `cv` or `rk` is the identity point, the digest is undefined and the transaction
+is invalid.
+
+## Fee digests
+
+For each covered bundle, let $\mathsf{cv}_{\mathsf{feeMax}}$ be its decompressed
+`cvFeeMaxTachyon`, $f$ its integer `vFeeTachyon` embedded in the Pallas base field,
+and $\mathsf{cm}_{\mathsf{chg}}$ the last entry of its `vTachygrams`. Its fee digest is
+
+$$d_{\mathsf{fee}} = \mathsf{Poseidon}_{\texttt{Tachyon-FeeDg}}\bigl(
+  x(\mathsf{cv}_{\mathsf{feeMax}}), y(\mathsf{cv}_{\mathsf{feeMax}}),
+  f, \mathsf{cm}_{\mathsf{chg}}\bigr).$$
+
+This digest binds the fee change commitment to its bundle's fee descriptor.
+The proof constraints are specified under
+[Fees](draft-tachyon-shielded-protocol.md#fees).[^tachyon-fees]
+
+## Action descriptor digests
+
+An action's descriptor is its 64-byte encoding in `vActionsTachyon`: the 32-byte encoding of $\mathsf{cv}$ followed by the 32-byte encoding of $\mathsf{rk}$.
+The descriptor digest of a sequence of actions is the BLAKE2b-256 hash, with personalization `Tachyon-Actions`, of the concatenation of their descriptors:
+
+$$\mathsf{h} = \text{BLAKE2b-256}\bigl(
+    \text{"Tachyon-Actions"},\ \mathsf{cv}_1 \| \mathsf{rk}_1 \| \cdots \| \mathsf{cv}_n \| \mathsf{rk}_n
+  \bigr)$$
+
+The digest of the empty sequence is the hash of the empty string under the same personalization.
+
+`hActionsTachyon` uses this construction over the bundle's own descriptors in
+their `vActionsTachyon` wire order. It contributes to the effecting digest and is
+not serialized. Tachygram pairs are excluded from this descriptor hash; the
+proof binds them through the separate [Action digests](#actiondigests).
+
+## Multiset commitments
+
+Multiset commitments MUST use the construction specified in the
+[Tachyon Shielded Protocol](draft-tachyon-shielded-protocol.md#multisetcommitments) ZIP.
+
+Validators reconstruct `cStampActionsTachyon` from every covered action digest and
+one fee digest per covered bundle. This commitment is not serialized. They also
+reconstruct `cTachygrams` from the union of those bundles' `vTachygrams` and MUST
+check it against the carried commitment. The proof binds both reconstructed
+multisets, as specified under [Block validity](#blockvalidity).
+
+## Proof stamp
+
+When `tachyonBundleState` is `0x01`, the proof stamp follows the body.
+
+`vTachygrams` contains only the carrying bundle's two tachygrams per action, in
+descriptor order, followed by its fee change note commitment. There is no
+separate tachygram count. These entries remain in the same transaction through
+aggregation and stripping.
+
+`vAdjunctsTachyon` lists the 32-byte `txid` of every other transaction covered by
+the proof. The carrying transaction is implicitly covered and MUST NOT appear
+in its own list. A proof covering only its carrying bundle has an empty list.
+Each listed transaction MUST be stripped and present in the same block.
+Every stripped bundle MUST be listed exactly once across the block's proof
+stamps, including bundles with no actions ([Block validity](#blockvalidity)).
+
+`anchorTachyon` references the pool state against which the proof is valid;
+anchor and epoch rules are specified in the shielded-protocol ZIP's
+[Per-stamp checks](draft-tachyon-shielded-protocol.md#per-stampchecks).
+`cTachygrams` commits to the union of the carrying bundle's tachygrams and those
+of the listed bundles. It MUST match the reconstructed commitment.
+
+For $N$ covered actions in $B$ covered bundles, the union has $2N + B$ members,
+all distinct, and MUST contain at most 8191 members. This bound follows from
+the production polynomial capacity of 8192 coefficients.[^tachyon-wire]
+
+`proofTachyon` is a Ragu-encoded proof of the shielded protocol's
+[Proof tree](draft-tachyon-shielded-protocol.md#prooftree) statements. Block
+validation MUST use the compressed consensus proof form. `sizeProofTachyon`
+gives its encoded byte length; a parser MUST reject lengths above the Ragu
+transport bound before allocating the proof buffer, and MUST reject invalid
+envelopes or lengths.[^tachyon-wire]
+
+TODO: Fix the Ragu proof-format version and numerical transport bound in the
+activating specification.
+
+The adjunct list is authorization data included in `auth_digest`. It is not
+signed or itself an input to the stamp proof. Validators MUST resolve the list
+and verify coverage against the actual bundles in the block. The proof binds
+their action pairs and fee descriptors, including the fee change commitments.
+[^tachyon-aggregation]
+
+## Stripped stamp
+
+When `tachyonBundleState` is `0x02`, the stripped trailer follows the body.
+It preserves the bundle's `vTachygrams` and `vFeeTachyon`. It contains no proof,
+anchor, tachygram-union commitment, or reference to a covering transaction.
+
+Stripping removes the proof stamp's additional fields without changing the body,
+tachygrams, or fee. The covering proof stamp identifies this transaction by its
+`txid`. See [Block validity](#blockvalidity) for coverage requirements.
+
+## Canonical encodings
+
+* Every compactSize field MUST use its minimal encoding and MUST NOT exceed
+  `0x02000000`; narrower bounds below also apply.
+* `nActionsTachyon` MUST be at most 4095. A proof-stamp parser MUST reject
+  `2 * nActionsTachyon + nAdjunctsTachyon + 2 > 8192` before reading the adjunct
+  list. Every covered bundle contributes at least its fee change tachygram.
+* `cv`, `rk`, and `cvFeeMaxTachyon` are 32-byte compressed Pallas points. Their
+  encodings MUST be canonical; `rk` MUST decode as a RedPallas validating key.
+  All three points MUST be non-identity.
+* `anchorTachyon` and each tachygram are canonical little-endian encodings of
+  Pallas base-field elements; encodings at least the field modulus MUST be rejected.
+* `vActionsTachyon` is in the author's chosen order. Signatures and tachygram
+  pairs follow the corresponding descriptor positions.
+* Each tachygram pair MAY appear in either order. The reference prover emits
+  the smaller member first, but parsing MUST preserve the received order.
+  Reordering a pair changes `auth_digest` without changing its action digest.
+  There is no global sort of `vTachygrams`.[^tachyon-wire]
+* `vAdjunctsTachyon` MUST be strictly ascending by bytewise comparison of txids.
+  A parser MUST reject repeats or a different order.
+* `cTachygrams` MUST be a canonical compressed non-identity Vesta point.
+  Whether it commits to the covered bundles' tachygrams is checked during
+  [block validation](#blockvalidity).
+* `vFeeTachyon` is an unsigned 64-bit little-endian integer and MUST NOT exceed
+  `MAX_MONEY`. `valueBalanceTachyon` is a signed 64-bit little-endian integer
+  in the inclusive range `-MAX_MONEY` to `MAX_MONEY`.
+* `vMemoTachyon` is opaque. Signatures are 64-byte strings whose validity is
+  checked during signature verification.
+* `proofTachyon` MUST satisfy the length and decoding rules in [Proof stamp](#proofstamp).
+
+## Transaction digest contributions
+
+The bundle contributes to both transaction digest trees in the ZIP 244
+framework.[^zip-0244] The following leaf constructions track PR #280;
+integration into the enclosing transaction format and assignment of its
+personalizations remain to be finalized.[^tachyon-identifiers]
+
+Let $H_p(m)$ denote BLAKE2b-256 of byte string $m$ with ASCII personalization
+$p$, zero-padded to 16 bytes. All concatenations below use the fields' wire
+encodings without compactSize count or length prefixes. An absent component
+uses the corresponding personalized hash of the empty byte string.
+
+### Effecting data
+
+`hActionsTachyon` is the descriptor digest in wire order, and
+$\mathsf{hMemoTachyon} = H_{\texttt{Tachyon-Memo}}(\mathsf{vMemoTachyon})$.
+The bundle's effecting contribution is
+
+$$H_{\texttt{ZTxIdTachyonHash}}\bigl(
+ \mathsf{hActionsTachyon} \| \mathsf{LE64}(\mathsf{valueBalanceTachyon})
+ \| \mathsf{cvFeeMaxTachyon} \| \mathsf{hMemoTachyon}\bigr).$$
+
+The trailer is excluded from `txid` and the sighash. In particular, tachygram
+pairs, the applied fee, and the adjunct list remain authorization data. Stamping,
+merging, stripping, and re-stamping preserve the effecting contribution.
+
+### Authorizing data
+
+Define the following 32-byte digests:
+
+$$\mathsf{hStampAdjunctsTachyon} = H_{\texttt{Tachyon-Adjuncts}}(
+  \mathsf{vAdjunctsTachyon}),$$
+
+$$\mathsf{hStampProofTachyon} = H_{\texttt{Tachyon-Proof}}(
+  \mathsf{anchorTachyon} \| \mathsf{cTachygrams} \| \mathsf{proofTachyon}).$$
+
+For a stripped stamp, both digests use empty input. For a proof stamp with no
+adjuncts, only the adjunct-list digest uses empty input. `proofTachyon` includes
+its Ragu envelope. Both stamp forms then contribute
+
+$$\mathsf{hStampTachyon} = H_{\texttt{Tachyon-Stamp}}\bigl(
+  \mathsf{vTachygrams} \| \mathsf{LE64}(\mathsf{vFeeTachyon})
+  \| \mathsf{hStampAdjunctsTachyon} \| \mathsf{hStampProofTachyon}\bigr).$$
+
+The bundle's authorizing contribution is
+
+$$H_{\texttt{ZTxAuthTachyHash}}\bigl(
+  \mathsf{tachyonBundleState} \| \mathsf{vActionSigsTachyon}
+  \| \mathsf{bindingSigTachyon} \| \mathsf{hStampTachyon}\bigr).$$
+
+For no Tachyon bundle, each contribution hashes empty input under its respective
+personalization. A present bundle with no actions remains distinct: it still
+contains its balance, maximum-fee commitment, binding signature, and trailer.
+
+`wtxid = txid || auth_digest` continues to identify a specific authorization
+form.[^zip-0239] A stripped bundle's `wtxid` depends only on that transaction;
+changing the covering aggregate does not rewrite the adjunct.
+
+## Bundle validity
+
+These checks apply to every bundle, including stripped bundles:
+
+1. The state byte, encodings, counts, ranges, and proof framing MUST satisfy
+   [Placement and bundle states](#placementandbundlestates) and
+   [Canonical encodings](#canonicalencodings).
+2. Every action signature MUST verify under its corresponding `rk`, and
+   `bindingSigTachyon` MUST verify under the derived binding key, over the
+   containing transaction's sighash.
+3. A bundle with no actions MUST have zero `valueBalanceTachyon` and zero
+   `vFeeTachyon`; its proof MUST establish a zero maximum fee. It still publishes
+   a fee change note commitment and requires proof coverage.
+4. The bundle's own `vTachygrams` MUST contain no repeated member.
+
+Signature checks apply independently to each covered bundle. Valid signatures
+and encodings do not establish proof coverage; the block rules below also apply.
+
+## Block validity
+
+A validator MUST enforce the following across all Tachyon bundles in a block:
+
+1. **Unique coverage.** Every txid listed by a proof stamp MUST identify a
+   transaction in the same block with a stripped Tachyon bundle. Every stripped
+   bundle MUST be listed by exactly one proof stamp. This applies even when it
+   has no actions. The carrying transaction is covered implicitly and MUST NOT
+   list itself. References to proof-stamped transactions are invalid.
+2. **Tachygram uniqueness.** Scan `vTachygrams` from every present bundle, including
+   stripped bundles. All members MUST be distinct across the block. Cross-block
+   duplicate checks use the shielded protocol's
+   [epoch window](draft-tachyon-shielded-protocol.md#per-stampchecks).
+3. **Coverage reconstruction.** For each proof stamp, collect its own bundle and
+   all bundles named by its adjunct list. Action descriptors MUST be distinct.
+   The 40-byte fee entries `cvFeeMaxTachyon || LE64(vFeeTachyon)` MUST also be
+   distinct. Associate each action with its own bundle's corresponding pair,
+   and each fee descriptor with that bundle's final tachygram. The resulting
+   union MUST contain at most 8191 tachygrams.
+4. **Tachygram commitment.** Reconstruct the multiset commitment to this union
+   and reject unless it equals the proof stamp's `cTachygrams`.
+5. **Proof verification.** Reconstruct the action/fee multiset commitment from
+   the [Action digests](#actiondigests) and [Fee digests](#feedigests). The Ragu
+   proof MUST verify against the reconstructed data and `anchorTachyon`, under
+   the shielded protocol's
+   [proof verification rules](draft-tachyon-shielded-protocol.md#per-stampchecks).
+
+A validator can enforce rule 1 by indexing all stripped bundles by txid, removing
+each as a proof stamp claims it, rejecting absent or already-claimed entries,
+and rejecting any entries left unclaimed. Checking only the lists would miss
+unlisted, unproved bundles. These checks belong to the node; the reference
+library's bundle verifier receives already-resolved adjuncts.[^tachyon-aggregation]
+
+After verification, the shielded protocol's
+[accumulator rules](draft-tachyon-shielded-protocol.md#tachygramaccumulator) advance
+pool state once per proof stamp using its covered union. Stripped bundles do not
+cause additional absorption of the same tachygrams.
+
+# Rationale
+
+This section is explanatory and introduces no additional protocol requirements.
+
+## Transaction-local tachygrams
+
+The action digest binds each pair to its action. Keeping those pairs on their
+originating transactions preserves that association after aggregation and permits
+retrieval by tachygram. The fee digest similarly binds the fee change commitment
+to its bundle.[^tachyon-design]
+
+## Aggregate references use txid
+
+The txid list identifies the transactions whose data are needed to verify the
+aggregate. A txid is stable across stripping; the proof binds the actual pairs,
+fees, and fee changes supplied for those transactions. A different authorization
+form with incompatible data fails verification. Stripped bundles need no
+reference rewritten when the aggregate is lifted, merged, or rerandomized.
+
+## Pair order and list order
+
+The sum/product action digest treats each tachygram pair as unordered. The wire
+format accepts either order and the authorization digest records the received
+bytes. The reference prover emits smaller-first pairs to avoid signaling their
+roles through order. Adjunct txids are strictly sorted to give their set one
+wire ordering.
+
+## Covered descriptors are distinct
+
+The multiset commitment preserves repeated roots; it does not prohibit them.
+Explicit checks reject repeated action and fee descriptors before proof
+verification. Parsers preserve action multiplicity and order.
+
+## Zero-action bundles still need coverage
+
+A zero-action bundle retains its maximum-fee commitment, binding signature,
+zero applied fee, and fee change tachygram. Its fee proof and block coverage
+remain necessary even though it contributes no ordinary action descriptors.
+
+## Deterministic multiset commitments
+
+The committed multisets are public, and deterministic commitments let validators
+reconstruct them from the covered bundles.
+
+# Security Implications
+
+This section is explanatory and introduces no additional protocol requirements.
+
+Signatures cover effecting data. Stripping preserves that data and the
+signatures, while changing `auth_digest` and `wtxid`. A valid binding signature
+enforces the value balance, including the maximum-fee commitment; the proof
+establishes the applied fee and the resulting fee change note.
+
+The adjunct list is included in `auth_digest`, but is not signed or itself bound
+by the proof. Nodes resolve it against the block, verify the actual covered
+bundles, and enforce exactly-once coverage. Omitting the check for unlisted
+stripped bundles would permit actions with no proof.[^tachyon-aggregation]
+
+Tachygrams remain authorization data, but their association with actions is
+enforced by the proof's action digests. Preserving the overall tachygram union
+while relocating members between actions does not preserve those digests.
+
+Parse validity and signature validity do not establish spend validity. The
+[Block validity](#blockvalidity) rules and the shielded protocol's
+[Consensus rules](draft-tachyon-shielded-protocol.md#consensusrules) also apply.
+
+# Privacy Implications
+
+This section is explanatory and introduces no additional protocol requirements.
+
+$\mathsf{cv}$ hides the action's value. The action count, value balance, applied
+fee, and each bundle's tachygrams are public. The wire order reveals which two
+tachygrams belong to each action and identifies the fee change commitment.
+An aggregate's txid list reveals its covered transactions.
+
+An action's pair does not label its members or distinguish a spend from an
+output in a single version. Comparing versions re-proved at different epochs
+can distinguish spends, whose pairs change, from outputs, whose pairs remain
+the same. See the shielded protocol's
+[Privacy and Security Implications](draft-tachyon-shielded-protocol.md#privacyandsecurityimplications).
+
+Key unlinkability and note privacy depend on the shielded protocol. Payload
+confidentiality and note discovery depend on the payment protocol.
+

+
+This ZIP will be deployed with [NuTachyon](draft-tachyon-nutachyon-upgrade.md).

+ZIP: XXX
+Title: Tachyon Shielded Protocol
+Owners: Connor O'Hara <connor@s1nus.com>
+Status: Draft
+Category: Consensus
+Created: 2026-09-23
+License: MIT
+```
+
+
+# Terminology
+
+The key word "MUST" in this document is to be interpreted as described in
+BCP 14 [^BCP14] when, and only when, it appears in all capitals.
+
+
+# Abstract
+
+This document proposes the Tachyon shielded protocol, which defines a new shielded pool with various scalability advantages. Tachyon enables validators to prune nullifier state, and supports aggregation of ZK proofs.
+Tachyon decouples note-encryption and transmission semantics from the shielded
+protocol, allowing more-scalable payment protocols to be built on top.
+
+# Motivation
+
+The Orchard shielded protocol specified by ZIP-224 introduced a proof system designed around a curve cycle, with two main motivations:
+
+- Removing the system's reliance on a "trusted setup", both to harden the trust assumptions of the shielded protocol and to remove the coordination complexity of the setup process.
+- Introduce the possibility of integrating known scaling techniques based on recursive zero-knowledge proofs in a future upgrade.
+
+While the first goal was achieved, the Orchard shielded protocol does not utilize Halo 2's recursion capability for a scalable protocol.
+
+We are thus motivated to deploy a new shielded protocol focused on scalability, fully utilizing recursive proofs to overcome two major bottlenecks:
+
+- Nullifier state growth:
+    - All of Zcash's existing shielded protocols have an unfortunate drawback of infinitely growing nullifier state. All validators must store the full historical nullifier set, the entirety of which must be retained to validate shielded transactions.
+    - This limits scalability, as raising the transaction throughput would result in linear growth of disk and memory requirements for validators.
+- Proof size and verification cost:
+    - Orchard uses a single proof per bundle, but its size grows linearly with the number
+      of actions. Proofs from separate transactions cannot be recursively combined under
+      the deployed protocol.[^zip-0225]
+    - Increasing transaction throughput therefore increases the proof data that validators
+      must receive and store, as well as their total proof-verification workload.
+    
+Tachyon remediates both bottlenecks by leveraging recursive proofs:
+- By requiring users to privately obtain and supply a recursive zero-knowledge proof of their notes spendability along with their transaction, nullifier state may be organized into [_epochs_](#epochs) and periodically pruned by validators.
+- By allowing proofs from multiple transactions to be aggregated into a single proof, storage and verification costs can be amortized for proof data.
+
+
+Tachyon decouples note transmission from the shielded protocol. The blockchain can still carry arbitrary payloads, but the Tachyon shielded protocol treats them as opaque rather than prescribing their encryption or note-transmission semantics. Higher-level payment protocols define how recipients discover and decrypt this data, and may use private information retrieval (PIR) to retrieve it privately.[^tachyon-secret-distribution] [^tachyon-payment-protocols]
+
+Encryption, transport, and discovery are not prescribed by this
+ZIP. This separation permits note transmission and discovery to evolve
+independently of consensus, including approaches that avoid scanning every
+transaction. [^tachyon-payment-protocols]
+
+# Specification
+
+The Tachyon protocol MUST be implemented as specified in the Zcash Protocol
+Specification.[^protocol-tachyon]
+
+This revision incorporates the transaction-local tachygrams and aggregate txid
+lists proposed in issue #226 and implemented in draft Tachyon PR #280 at revision
+`e6bcdf1`.[^tachyon-design] [^tachyon-format-pr]
+
+
+## Curves and fields
+
+Tachyon retains the Pallas / Vesta (Pasta) curve cycle and finite fields used by
+Orchard, as described in ZIP 224.[^zip-0224] The base field of each curve is the
+scalar field of the other; their parameters are unchanged.[^protocol-pallasandvesta]
+
+Pallas remains the application curve, used for RedPallas signatures and value
+commitments. Unlike Orchard's non-recursive use of Halo 2, Tachyon's Ragu proving
+system utilizes the full curve cycle for recursive proof composition.[^ragu]
+
+## Proving system
+
+Tachyon uses the Ragu proving system,[^ragu] with R1CS-like arithmetization inspired by Bootle16[^bootle16], efficient recursion via split accumulation, and its online polynomial oracle and transcript bridging features.[^bclms21]
+
+## Tachygrams
+
+Tachyon unifies the consensus treatment of note commitments, nullifiers, and
+padding values as Pallas base-field elements called _tachygrams_. A spend
+contributes its nullifiers for the spending epoch and the following epoch; an
+output contributes its note commitment and a padding tachygram. Both action
+types contribute two values.
+
+Each transaction publishes its own action pairs, in action order, followed by
+one fee change note commitment. These tachygrams remain with that transaction
+when its proof is aggregated or stripped. The proof binds each unordered pair
+to its action through the [action digest](draft-tachyon-bundle-format.md#actiondigests),
+and the fee change commitment through the
+[fee digest](draft-tachyon-bundle-format.md#feedigests).
+
+Pair membership and the fee change commitment are public. An action's pair
+does not label its members or distinguish spends from outputs in a single
+version. Consensus applies the same duplicate-rejection rules to all tachygrams
+and reconstructs their union for each covering stamp.[^tachyon-tachygrams]
+
+## Stamp
+
+A stamp packages a recursive zero-knowledge proof, a pool-state anchor, and a
+commitment to the tachygram union of its covered bundles. The proof binds the
+covered actions to their tachygram pairs and establishes the corresponding
+note-creation, spendability, and fee statements.[^protocol-tachyon-stamp-verification]
+
+A stamp can cover one transaction or aggregate multiple transactions.
+[Aggregation](#prooftree) merges their proofs while actions, signatures, tachygrams,
+and applied fees remain in their respective transactions. The covering
+transaction lists the txids of the other transactions it covers. Its own bundle
+is covered implicitly.[^tachyon-proof-tree]
+
+The bundle-format ZIP specifies the [proof stamp](draft-tachyon-bundle-format.md#proofstamp)
+and [stripped stamp](draft-tachyon-bundle-format.md#strippedstamp) encodings and
+[block validation](draft-tachyon-bundle-format.md#blockvalidity), which requires
+every stripped bundle to be covered exactly once.
+
+## Epochs
+
+An epoch is a fixed-length interval of consecutive blocks, identified by an index derived from block height. Each note has a deterministic nullifier for each epoch, independent of the choice of anchor. A spend referencing a pool state in epoch $e$ publishes the note’s nullifiers for epochs $e$ and $e+1$, allowing inclusion across an epoch boundary.[^tachyon-nullifiers]
+
+When validating a transaction, validators check for duplicate nullifiers in the
+current and immediately preceding epochs. Recursive spendability proofs cover
+earlier history, allowing validators to prune older nullifier state from their
+active duplicate-checking set.
+[^tachyon-tachygrams] [^tachyon-proof-tree]
+
+Epoch boundaries and cross-epoch validation rules MUST be implemented as specified
+in the Zcash Protocol Specification.[^protocol-tachyon-epochs]
+
+
+## Proof tree
+
+Instead of Orchard's single action circuit, Tachyon uses a recursive proof tree of
+specialized proof-carrying data (PCD) steps. Each step enforces its own constraints and recursively verifies up to two input PCD proofs, producing a new folded PCD proof.
+
+Spend proofs combine evidence of note creation, correct per-epoch nullifier
+derivation, and continued unspentness up to an anchor. Separate output steps prove
+correct construction of new notes. The resulting proofs bind an anchor, the action
+digests, and the tachygram multiset. Each action digest includes its unordered pair through the
+pair's sum and product. Fee steps additionally bind one fee digest and fee change
+note commitment per covered bundle.[^tachyon-direct-binding]
+
+Stamps at a common anchor can be merged recursively, first to cover a transaction's
+actions and then to aggregate independently constructed transactions. Before merging, anyone with the published transaction and chain data (likely a miner or other aggregator) can use anchor-span proofs to lift stamps to a later anchor within the same spending epoch, enabling them to be merged during aggregation. Validators check the resulting proof against commitments reconstructed from the
+covered action pairs, fee descriptors, and the union of the covered bundles'
+tachygrams, and check the anchor against chain state.
+
+- PCD step statements and composition rules: [^protocol-tachyon-proof-tree]
+- Stamp public inputs and verification: [^protocol-tachyon-stamp-verification]
+- Design description: [^tachyon-proof-tree]
+
+## Commitment schemes
+
+Tachyon retains Orchard's homomorphic Pedersen value commitments on Pallas,
+including the value and randomness generators. A Tachyon action commits to a
+signed value, positive for spends and negative for outputs.
+
+For the note structure and Poseidon note commitment, see
+[Notes and note commitments](#notesandnotecommitments).
+
+- Value commitment scheme: [^protocol-valuecommit]
+- Design and implementation: [^tachyon-authorization]
+
+### Multiset commitments
+
+Tachyon uses deterministic Pedersen polynomial commitments on Vesta for
+action and fee digests and for tachygram multisets. A multiset of Pallas base-field
+elements is encoded by taking its members as the roots of a monic polynomial. For action and fee
+digests $d_i$ and tachygrams $t_j$:
+
+$$A(X) = \prod_i \bigl(X - d_i\bigr) \qquad
+T(X) = \prod_j \bigl(X - t_j\bigr)$$
+
+The commitment to a polynomial of degree $n$ is the deterministic, untrapdoored
+Pedersen commitment to its $n+1$ coefficients over the Vesta group, using the
+polynomial-commitment generators fixed by Ragu, with no blinding term. The
+coefficients are ordered by ascending degree: the constant term pairs with $G_0$,
+and the degree-$k$ coefficient pairs with $G_k$.
+
+A polynomial is invariant under permutation of its roots, and a repeated member
+becomes a repeated root. These commitments therefore preserve multiplicity but
+not order. They are deterministic functions of the public multisets and reveal
+no information beyond those multisets.
+
+The multiset commitment construction MUST be implemented as specified in the
+Zcash Protocol Specification.[^protocol-tachyon-multisetcommit]
+Design and implementation: [^tachyon-multisetcommit].
+
+
+## Tachygram accumulator
+
+Tachyon unifies the history represented by Orchard's note commitment tree and
+nullifier set in a single accumulator over [tachygrams](#tachygrams): note
+commitments, nullifiers, and padding values.
+
+The construction is a Poseidon hash chain of smaller multiset accumulators, one
+per proof stamp. Each commitment to the covered bundles' tachygram union is
+absorbed once into the chain, which also records epoch transitions, to derive
+pool-state anchors. Validators
+still retain recent tachygrams for the duplicate checks described under
+[Epochs](#epochs).
+
+The tachygram accumulator MUST be implemented as specified in the Zcash Protocol
+Specification.[^protocol-tachyon-accumulator]
+
+
+## Keys and addresses
+
+Tachyon's key design deliberately stays close to Orchard. It retains the 32-byte
+spending key $\mathsf{sk}$, derivation of the spend-authorizing key $\mathsf{ask}$
+and base-field nullifier key $\mathsf{nk}$, and RedPallas spend authorization with
+a spend-validating key $\mathsf{ak}$ and randomized per-spend keys.
+
+The principal changes are:
+
+- The proof-authorizing key is explicitly represented as
+  $\mathsf{pak} = (\mathsf{ak}, \mathsf{nk})$, allowing proof construction without
+  the spend-authorizing key.
+- The per-action randomizer $\alpha$ MUST be derived from the note commitment
+  $\mathsf{cm}$ and per-action entropy using a domain-separated derivation. For a
+  spend, the randomized spend-validating key
+  $\mathsf{rk} = \mathsf{ak} + [\alpha]\mathcal{G}$ therefore binds the action's
+  signed effecting data to the underlying note, even though its tachygrams are
+  carried separately in its own bundle's stamp trailer.[^tachyon-action-authorization]
+- The recipient is represented by a field-element payment key $\mathsf{pk}$,
+  derived from $\mathsf{ak}$ and $\mathsf{nk}$ using domain-separated Poseidon,
+  in place of Orchard's diversifier and diversified transmission key.
+- Orchard's viewing-key and diversified-address machinery is omitted from the
+  core protocol. Address management, viewing capabilities, transmission keys,
+  note encryption, and retrieval are instead defined by higher-level payment
+  protocols. Encrypted notes can still be published as opaque on-chain
+  payloads.[^tachyon-payment-protocols]
+
+Key components and derivation: [^protocol-tachyon-keys].
+Design and implementation: [^tachyon-keys] [^tachyon-key-derivation].
+
+
+## Notes and note commitments
+
+A Tachyon note has the form $(\mathsf{pk}, v, \psi, \mathsf{rcm})$, where
+$\mathsf{pk}$ is the recipient's payment key, $v$ is a non-negative value in
+zatoshis, $\psi$ is the nullifier trapdoor, and $\mathsf{rcm}$ is note-commitment
+randomness. The payment key, nullifier trapdoor, and commitment randomness are Pallas base-field elements. The value is a non-negative integer amount in zatoshis, also encoded as a field element when computing the commitment. Unlike
+Orchard, the note has no $\rho$ field linking it to the nullifier of a spend in
+the same action.[^tachyon-notes]
+
+The note commitment is a field element computed using domain-separated Poseidon
+in place of Orchard's Sinsemilla construction:
+
+$$\mathsf{cm} = \mathsf{Poseidon}_{\texttt{Tachyon-CmDerive}}(\mathsf{rcm}, \mathsf{pk}, v, \psi).$$
+
+An output action publishes $\mathsf{cm}$ together with a padding tachygram. [^tachyon-note-implementation] [^tachyon-tachygrams]
+The note structure and commitment MUST be implemented as specified in the Zcash
+Protocol Specification.[^protocol-tachyon-notecommit]
+
+
+## Nullifiers
+
+Unlike Orchard's fixed nullifier per note, Tachyon uses _evolving nullifiers_,
+deriving a different nullifier for each [epoch](#epochs).[^evolving-nullifiers]
+A per-note master key $\mathsf{mk}$ is derived from the note's $\psi$ and the
+recipient's nullifier key $\mathsf{nk}$. Abstractly:
+
+$$\mathsf{mk} = \mathsf{Poseidon}_{\texttt{Tachyon-NfMaster}}(\psi, \mathsf{nk}),$$
+
+$$\mathsf{nf}_e = \mathsf{PRF}^{\mathsf{nfTachyon}}_{\mathsf{mk}}(e).$$
+
+The PRF uses a domain-separated Poseidon sponge to derive groups of consecutive
+epochs' nullifiers. Its outputs are Pallas base-field elements.[^tachyon-nullifiers]
+
+A spend publishes $\mathsf{nf}_e$ and $\mathsf{nf}_{e+1}$, where $e$ is the epoch
+of its referenced pool state. The proof establishes that the note's applicable
+nullifiers were absent between its creation and that state; validators check for their non-existence in the retained tachygrams. This combines proofs of historical unspentness with a prunable consensus nullifier
+set.[^tachyon-proof-tree]
+
+Nullifier derivation and its proof constraints MUST be implemented as specified
+in the Zcash Protocol Specification.[^protocol-tachyon-nullifiers]
+
+
+## Fees
+
+Each bundle reserves a maximum fee in a max-fee note, represented publicly by
+its value commitment. The transaction's signatures bind this commitment. A
+fee at or below the maximum is selected after signing; the remainder becomes
+a fee change note with the same payment key, nullifier trapdoor, and commitment
+randomness. Its note commitment is the bundle's final tachygram, including when
+the change value is zero.[^tachyon-fees]
+
+The proof MUST establish the maximum-fee commitment's derivation from the note
+opening, the applied fee's range, and the fee change note's correct construction.
+Its fee digest includes the maximum-fee commitment, applied fee, and fee change
+commitment. A bundle with no actions has a zero maximum and applied fee, but
+still contributes its fee digest and fee change tachygram to the covering proof.
+
+Fee derivation and proof constraints MUST be implemented as specified in the
+Zcash Protocol Specification.[^protocol-tachyon-fees] The bundle-format ZIP
+specifies their [encoding and balance accounting](draft-tachyon-bundle-format.md#valuebalanceandthebindingsignature).
+
+
+## Consensus rules
+
+Tachyon consensus validation MUST be implemented as specified in the Zcash
+Protocol Specification.[^protocol-tachyon-consensus] The following summary groups
+the principal checks by what they validate: each transaction's bundle, or a stamp covering
+one or more bundles. Aggregation combines stamp proofs, but does not eliminate
+the checks on individual bundles.
+
+### Per-bundle checks
+
+The bundle-format ZIP's [Bundle validity](draft-tachyon-bundle-format.md#bundlevalidity)
+rules apply to every bundle, whether it carries a proof or is stripped. In summary:
+
+- Bundle fields have canonical encodings and satisfy their type and range
+  constraints. Each action's value commitment and authorization key, and each
+  bundle's maximum-fee commitment, are non-identity Pallas points. A bundle with
+  no actions has zero value balance and zero applied fee.
+- Every action signature and the bundle's binding signature verify over the
+  containing transaction's signature hash. The binding signature enforces
+  consistency between the action and maximum-fee commitments and the declared
+  value balance.
+- Opaque payment-protocol payloads satisfy the
+  [canonical encoding rules](draft-tachyon-bundle-format.md#canonicalencodings), and
+  their bytes are committed by the transaction's signature hash as described under
+  [Transaction digest contributions](draft-tachyon-bundle-format.md#transactiondigestcontributions).
+
+### Per-stamp checks
+
+These checks apply to each proof-bearing stamp, using all bundles it covers.
+The bundle-format ZIP's [Block validity](draft-tachyon-bundle-format.md#blockvalidity)
+section specifies block-scoped coverage and proof-verification procedures.
+The anchor, epoch-window, and accumulator rules below additionally depend on chain
+state.
+
+- Each proof stamp covers its own bundle and the stripped bundles named by its
+  txid list in the same block. Every stripped bundle is listed exactly once.
+- Covered action descriptors and fee entries are distinct. The covered tachygram
+  union has two members per action plus one fee change commitment per bundle.
+- Each stamp proof verifies against its anchor and the multiset commitments
+  reconstructed from the covered action pairs, fee descriptors, and tachygrams.
+- Each stamp anchor identifies an accepted end-of-block pool state in the
+  epoch of the block being validated or the immediately preceding epoch.
+- The tachygrams published by all bundles, including stripped bundles, are
+  distinct within the block and from tachygrams published in earlier blocks of the
+  current or immediately preceding epoch. This check treats note commitments,
+  nullifiers, and padding identically.
+- Each proof stamp advances the pool-state accumulator once with its covered
+  union, in transaction order, with epoch transitions incorporated as specified under
+  [Tachygram accumulator](#tachygramaccumulator).
+
+# Privacy and Security Implications
+
+Each transaction publicly identifies its own tachygrams, the pair associated
+with each action, and its fee change commitment. The proof enforces these
+associations, which support retrieval by tachygram after aggregation. Aggregate
+txid lists also reveal which transactions share a covering proof.[^tachyon-design]
+
+The pair alone does not distinguish a spend from an output in a single version.
+Re-proving a spend at another epoch changes its nullifier pair, while an output's
+pair remains unchanged; comparing versions can therefore distinguish the action
+types. This is additional information exposed by public pairing.[^tachyon-tachygrams]
+
+Confidential note transmission, recipient authentication, and note discovery are
+responsibilities of the chosen payment protocol. On-chain payloads are publicly
+visible, so the confidentiality of encrypted note data depends on that protocol's
+encryption scheme. Retrieval privacy is distinct: PIR can hide which records a
+recipient requests from a retrieval service, but does not conceal the published
+ciphertexts or, by itself, all network metadata.
+
+A valid shielded proof does not establish that the intended recipient has
+received or can recover the note opening. Privacy against network observers and
+leakage through payment metadata also depend on the higher-level payment
+protocol.[^tachyon-payment-protocols]
+
+# Non-requirements
+
+This ZIP does not prescribe P2P aggregation messages, covered-transaction discovery,
+or mempool and relay policy. 
+
+The Tachyon shielded protocol is unopinionated about the payment protocols
+constructed on top of it. This ZIP does not prescribe payment-address formats,
+note encryption, incoming-note discovery, selective disclosure, or a retrieval
+mechanism.
+
+On-chain publication and off-chain retrieval are separate concerns. A payment
+protocol may publish encrypted notes on the ledger and retrieve them through
+off-chain services, or use out-of-band note transmission instead. This ZIP
+requires neither PIR nor a particular payment protocol; the resulting shielded
+transactions still satisfy Tachyon's consensus rules.[^tachyon-payment-protocols]
+
+# Deployment
+
+The Tachyon shielded protocol will be deployed with
+[NuTachyon](draft-tachyon-nutachyon-upgrade.md).
+
+
+# Reference Implementation
+
+The [Tachyon repository](https://github.com/tachyon-zcash/tachyon) implements the
+shielded protocol in Rust, using the recursive proof-carrying data framework in
+the [Ragu repository](https://github.com/tachyon-zcash/ragu). Experimental
+full-node integration is provided by
+[Zakura PR #795](https://github.com/zakura-core/zakura/pull/795), with corresponding
+transaction-format, digest, value-accounting, and history-tree support in [zakura-core/common PR #178](https://github.com/zakura-core/common/pull/178).
+
+Direct action-to-tachygram binding and aggregate txid lists are implemented in
+[Tachyon PR #280](https://github.com/tachyon-zcash/tachyon/pull/280), revision
+`e6bcdf1`. That PR is an unmerged draft; the earlier node integrations require
+corresponding updates for this format.
